title: Rabbit Model for Supraspinatus Tendon Defect and Scaffold-Assisted Repair
author: Huang, Tam, et al.
materials: Surgical instruments
Sterile gloves
Ketamine
Xylazine
Betadine
70% ethanol
Cotton swabs
Gauze
Medical tape
No.15 scalpel
Saline solution
3 − 0 suture
Arthrex FiberWire®
Scaffold
Surgical instruments were autoclave-sterilized, and sterile gloves were worn throughout the procedure, which was carried out in a sterile operating field.
Anesthesia was induced in both female and male New Zealand White Rabbits by administering an intramuscular injection of a ketamine (35 mg/kg; Alfasan) and xylazine (5 mg/kg; Alfasan) mixture.

To maintain anesthesia in rabbits during the surgery, a 5 ml syringe containing the ketamine (35 mg/kg) and xylazine (5 mg/kg) mixture was prepared. The rabbit’s ear vein was located, and an indwelling needle was carefully inserted and connected to the syringe containing the anesthetic. The syringe was secured with gauze and medical tape.

The anesthetized rabbit was gently positioned in a supine position, ensuring that the surgical area faced upwards. The surgical area was shaved and cleansed by applying three alternating applications of betadine and 70% ethanol, applied in circular motions, starting from the inside and moving outward, using a cotton swab. Surgical drapes were placed to create a surgical window and maintain a sterile environment.

A 3 cm incision was made in the shoulder to expose the rotator cuff tendons. The deltoid muscle was split, and skin and soft tissue retractors were used to create a surgical window, providing a clear view of the rotator cuff tissues. Acromioplasty was performed using a No.15 scalpel (Mingyue). Hemostasis was achieved, and the wound was irrigated with saline solution.
The supraspinatus tendon was identified and marked using a 3 − 0 suture (Arthrex FiberWire®). The supraspinatus tendon was sutured using a lock-loop suturing technique before detaching it.

A full-thickness defect, measuring approximately 10 × 5 mm, was created in the mid-substance of the supraspinatus tendon using a No.15 scalpel. The distance between the defect and the first lock-loop suture site was approximately 1–2 mm. The opposite end of the supraspinatus tendon was sutured using the lock-loop suturing method.

To achieve a secure attachment between the scaffold and the tendon, a modified Mason-Allen suture technique was utilized. After completing the lock-loop suture, all subsequent sutures were positioned behind the lock-loop to minimize the risk of suture pull-out. Prior to the surgical procedure, three holes were created in the scaffold. The dimensions of the scaffold were designed to closely resemble the width and thickness of the native rabbit supraspinatus tendon.

The first stitch was passed through one-third of the tendon’s width and then secured with a knot, using its own suture as the initial fixation. The second stitch emerged behind the first stitch and connected to one of the scaffold’s holes, forming a stable “cross” structure between the first and second stitches.

After the suture was passed through the scaffold, it traversed the tendon from behind the lock-loop suture. At this stage, the Mason-Allen method was employed to tie a “cross” knot at two-thirds of the tendon’s length, while simultaneously connecting the tensioned suture to the second hole of the scaffold. Following the final Mason-Allen knot, an additional knot was tied using the suture itself at the opposing end of the tendon, to enhance fixation of the scaffold-tendon connection. The same suturing technique was employed to secure the scaffold and tendon together at the other end of the tendon.
After the implantation, post-surgery analgesic (0.01-0.05 mg/kg Buprenorphine, Alfasan) was administered subcutaneously to ensure pain relief for the rabbits.
To prevent infection, an anti-infective (20 mg/kg Cefalexin, Alfasan) was administered.
A suture (3 − 0 PGA) was used to carefully reapproximate the deltoid muscle tissue layer by layer, and the skin was closed with 3 − 0 silk sutures.
To sterilize the wound and clean up any blood, betadine was applied in circular motions using a cotton swab, starting from the inside and moving outward.
The rabbits were allowed to recover on a heating pad and subsequently allowed cage activity in their cages without immobilization.

At the designated time point of postoperative 1 month, euthanasia was performed on the rabbits using a lethal dose of sodium pentobarbital (Alfasan), administered at a dosage of 60 mg/kg. Euthanasia was carried out in strict adherence to institutional animal ethics guidelines to ensure humane treatment of the animals.

steps.title: Sterilize instruments and wear gloves
steps.instruction: Autoclave‑sterilize all surgical instruments and put on sterile gloves before entering the sterile operating field.

steps.title: Induce and maintain anesthesia
steps.instruction: Give each rabbit an intramuscular injection of ketamine 35 mg/kg and xylazine 5 mg/kg (Alfasan). Prepare a 5 mL syringe with the same ketamine/xylazine mixture, insert an indwelling needle into the ear vein, connect the syringe, and secure it with gauze and medical tape for continuous anesthesia during surgery.

substeps.instruction: Inject ketamine 35 mg/kg IM.
Inject xylazine 5 mg/kg IM.
Prepare 5 mL syringe with ketamine 35 mg/kg + xylazine 5 mg/kg.
Locate ear vein, insert indwelling needle, attach syringe.
Secure needle with gauze and medical tape.

steps.title: Prepare and drape surgical site
steps.instruction: Place the anesthetized rabbit supine, shave the shoulder area, and clean it with three alternating applications of betadine and 70 % ethanol in circular motions from the inside outward using a cotton swab. Then apply sterile surgical drapes to create a sterile window.

substeps.instruction: Position rabbit supine with surgical area upward.
Shave the shoulder region.
Apply betadine, then 70 % ethanol, repeat three times in circular motions from inside outward with a cotton swab.
Place sterile drapes to form a surgical window.

steps.title: Incise shoulder and perform acromioplasty
steps.instruction: Make a 3 cm shoulder incision, split the deltoid muscle, use skin and soft‑tissue retractors to create a window, perform acromioplasty with a No.15 scalpel (Mingyue), achieve hemostasis, and irrigate the wound with saline solution.

substeps.instruction: Make 3 cm incision over the shoulder.
Split deltoid muscle.
Insert retractors to expose rotator cuff.
Perform acromioplasty using No.15 scalpel (Mingyue).
Control bleeding (hemostasis).
Irrigate wound with saline.

steps.title: Mark tendon and place lock‑loop suture
steps.instruction: Identify the supraspinatus tendon, mark it with a 3‑0 suture (Arthrex FiberWire®), and place a lock‑loop suture on the tendon before detaching it.

substeps.instruction: Identify supraspinatus tendon.
Mark tendon with 3‑0 Arthrex FiberWire® suture.
Place lock‑loop suture on tendon.
Detach tendon after suturing.

steps.title: Create tendon defect and opposite suturing
steps.instruction: Using a No.15 scalpel, create a full‑thickness defect measuring approximately 10 × 5 mm in the mid‑substance of the supraspinatus tendon; keep the defect 1–2 mm from the first lock‑loop suture site, and place a lock‑loop suture on the opposite tendon end.

substeps.instruction: Create 10 × 5 mm full‑thickness defect with No.15 scalpel.
Ensure defect is 1–2 mm from first lock‑loop suture.
Suture opposite tendon end with lock‑loop technique.

steps.title: Prepare scaffold with pre‑made holes
steps.instruction: Before surgery, create three holes in the scaffold; design the scaffold dimensions to match the width and thickness of the native rabbit supraspinatus tendon.

steps.title: Attach scaffold using modified Mason‑Allen
steps.instruction: After the lock‑loop suture, place all subsequent sutures behind it. Pass the first stitch through one‑third of the tendon width and tie a knot using its own suture. Pass the second stitch behind the first and connect it to one scaffold hole, forming a cross. Tie a Mason‑Allen “cross” knot at two‑thirds tendon length, linking the tensioned suture to the second scaffold hole, then add an extra knot at the opposite tendon end. Repeat the same technique at the other tendon end.

substeps.instruction: Place subsequent sutures behind lock‑loop suture.
First stitch: pass through one‑third tendon width, knot with its own suture.
Second stitch: pass behind first stitch, attach to scaffold hole, create cross.
Tie Mason‑Allen cross knot at two‑thirds tendon length, connect to second scaffold hole.
Add additional knot at opposing tendon end using same suture.
Repeat Mason‑Allen fixation at the other tendon end.

steps.title: Close muscle and skin layers
steps.instruction: Reapproximate the deltoid muscle layer‑by‑layer with 3‑0 PGA sutures, then close the skin with 3‑0 silk sutures.

substeps.instruction: Close deltoid muscle using 3‑0 PGA sutures, layer by layer.
Close skin using 3‑0 silk sutures.

steps.title: Apply final wound antiseptic
steps.instruction: Apply betadine in circular motions with a cotton swab, starting from the inside and moving outward, to sterilize the wound and clean any residual blood.

steps.title: Administer analgesic and antibiotic
steps.instruction: Give a subcutaneous injection of buprenorphine 0.01–0.05 mg/kg for analgesia and administer cefalexin 20 mg/kg (Alfasan) as an anti‑infective.

substeps.instruction: Inject buprenorphine 0.01–0.05 mg/kg SC.
Inject cefalexin 20 mg/kg SC.

steps.title: Recover animal and allow activity
steps.instruction: Place the rabbit on a heating pad until it recovers, then return it to its cage for unrestricted cage activity without immobilization.

substeps.instruction: Recover on heating pad.
Return to cage; allow free activity.

steps.title: Euthanize at one month post‑op
steps.instruction: At 1 month after surgery, euthanize each rabbit with a lethal dose of sodium pentobarbital 60 mg/kg (Alfasan) following institutional animal‑ethics guidelines.

substeps.instruction: Inject sodium pentobarbital 60 mg/kg IV/IM as lethal dose.
Confirm death according to ethics protocol.

steps.title: Fix harvested tissue in paraformaldehyde
steps.instruction: Immediately immerse the harvested samples in 4 % (w/v) paraformaldehyde (Sigma) for 48 hours fixation.

steps.title: Dehydrate, embed, and section tissue
steps.instruction: Pass the fixed samples through a graded ethanol series, embed them in paraffin blocks, then cut 7 µm sections and deparaffinize.

substeps.instruction: Dehydrate through graded ethanol.
Embed in paraffin.
Section at 7 µm thickness.
Deparaffinize sections.

steps.title: Stain sections with H&E and Picrosirius
steps.instruction: Stain the deparaffinized sections with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and with Picrosirius red.

steps.title: Image stained sections
steps.instruction: Examine H&E‑stained sections under bright‑field optics and Picrosirius‑red sections under polarized optics using a Nikon Ni‑U Eclipse Upright Microscope; capture images with a Nikon DSFi3 digital camera.

substeps.instruction: View H&E sections with bright‑field optics.
View Picrosirius sections with polarized optics.
Capture images using Nikon DSFi3 camera.

steps.title: Score H&E sections with histopathology scale
steps.instruction: Evaluate each H&E section for cellularity, vascularization, inflammation, and collagen alignment on a 0–3 semi‑quantitative scale; compute the average score for each parameter per group for comparison.

substeps.instruction: Score cellularity 0–3.
Score vascularization 0–3.
Score inflammation 0–3.
Score collagen alignment 0–3.
Calculate average scores per group.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Express data as mean ± SEM, compare groups using the Kruskal‑Wallis test followed by Mann‑Whitney U post‑hoc pairwise comparisons; denote significance as * p < 0.05, ** p < 0.01, *** p < 0.001, **** p < 0.0001.

substeps.instruction: Calculate mean ± SEM.
Run Kruskal‑Wallis test.
If significant, perform Mann‑Whitney U pairwise tests.
Annotate significance levels (*, **, ***, ****).
